newsitem.title: USA: KCBT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER, EXPORTS SEEN PICKING UP.
newsitem.headline: KCBT WHEAT CLOSES HIGHER, EXPORTS SEEN PICKING UP.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter closed sharply higher supported by short covering and talk that U.S. exports should start to pick up soon.
Dealers said the U.S. currently faced little competition in the export market with the European Union appearing reluctant to issue export licenses.
They noted there were few confirmed tenders but some talk that Egypt may be among the buyers entering the market soon.
September closed 9-3/4 cents a bushel higher at $3.73 a bushel while other positions finished with gains of 9-3/4 to 6-1/4 cents.

Floor sources said key buyers included E.D. and F. Man International (1.3 million bushels September), FCC (1.0 million September), FIMAT (1.0 million September) and Benson Quinn (1.0 million December).
Featured sellers included Benson Quinn (1.0 million bushels September) and General Mills (1.0 million September).
Volume was estimated at 31.8 million bushels, slightly up from the previous day's 28.3 million.
